claim: Trujillo is 45.6 km / ~32 min by car from Cáceres; Mérida 74 km / 55 min (37 min by train); Monfragüe 63.1 km / 54 min; Plasencia 79.9 km / 49 min.
quote: Trujillo ... 45.6 km ... 32 minutes ... Mérida ... 74 km ... 55 minutes (or 37 min by train) ... Monfragüe National Park ... 63.1 km ... 54 minutes ... Plasencia ... 79.9 km ... 49 minutes

claim: Trujillo is the birthplace of Francisco Pizarro (born 1478), conqueror of the Inca Empire, with a Plaza Mayor of Renaissance palaces funded by Peruvian silver and a 9th-century castle.
quote: Francisco Pizarro, the Spanish conquistador who conquered the Inca Empire, was born in Trujillo in 1478 ... The Renaissance palaces surrounding the Plaza Mayor were built by conquistador families using American silver and gold.

claim: Mérida's Archaeological Ensemble was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993 and includes a bridge over the Guadiana, an amphitheatre, a theatre, a vast circus and a water-supply system.
quote: The well-preserved remains include a large bridge over the Guadiana, an amphitheatre, a theatre, a vast circus and an exceptional water-supply system.

claim: Monfragüe National Park, ~60 km NE of Cáceres, holds one of the largest black vulture colonies in the world; the Salto del Gitano cliff (300 m) is its premier viewpoint for griffon vultures, black vultures, Egyptian vultures and black storks.
quote: The best place to see vultures and other birds in Monfragüe is from the 'Salto del Gitano' natural viewing point, on a cliff 300 metres high.

claim: Salto del Gitano holds the park's largest griffon vulture colony (~80 pairs) and regularly produces black stork, black vulture, Egyptian vulture, peregrine and blue rock thrush; early morning is best.
quote: Black Stork, Black Vulture, Griffon Vulture, Peregrine, Egyptian Vulture, Blue Rock Thrush, Rock Bunting, Red-rumped Swallow ... Salto del Gitano holds the park's largest colony of Griffon Vulture (approximately 80 pairs).

claim: The Royal Monastery of Santa María de Guadalupe (UNESCO 1993) blends Gothic and Mudéjar architecture, is the shrine of the Virgin of Guadalupe, and was where Columbus made his first pilgrimage after 1492 — giving its name to the Caribbean Guadeloupe.
quote: It was here in Extremadura where Christopher Columbus made his first pilgrimage after discovering America in 1492 ... Mudéjar cloister (1389–1405) ... late Gothic cloister from 1531–1533.

claim: Guadalupe lies barely 120 km from Cáceres, reached via the EX-206 toward Trujillo/Guadalupe.
quote: Barely 120 kilometres from Cáceres you will find a place full of legends ... take the exit for the EX-206 towards Trujillo/Guadalupe.

claim: The Valle del Jerte (between Plasencia and the Sierra de Gredos) has over 1.5 million cherry trees whose white 'Cerezo en Flor' bloom (a Festival of National Tourist Interest) runs roughly late March to early May; Cáceres to Cabezuela del Valle is ~115 km.
quote: The Jerte Valley is home to more than 1.5 million cherry trees ... From Cáceres to Cabezuela del Valle there are 115 km ... the bloom is likely to arrive between late March and early April.
